text: A royal lady had been reading the letter in her room when another important person, from whom she wished to hide it, suddenly entered. <break time="0.8s" /> Failing to push it into a drawer, she left it open on the table, with the address on top. <break time="0.8s" /> The Minister D, came in, and he at once noticed the letter, recognized the handwriting, and guessed her secret from her nervous face. <break time="0.8s" /> Laying a similar letter of his own beside it, he later took hers, and she dared not stop him with the other person present. <break time="0.8s" /> Hoping to get the letter back, the Prefect had searched the Ministers house every night for three months, the Minister being often away. <break time="0.8s" /> His men had opened every drawer, drilled into the legs of every chair, and examined each page of every book in the house. <break time="0.8s" /> Twice the Minister had even been stopped by fake robbers and searched, but the letter was nowhere to be found. <break time="0.8s" /> When Dupin said the Minister was no fool, the Prefect answered that he was a poet, which he thought was nearly the same thing. <break time="0.8s" /> Dupins only advice was to search the house again thoroughly, and the Prefect left us, looking more unhappy than I had ever seen him.
